02-read-date.js.attempt: read Date, for a wall clock

05-read-self.js.attempt: name the global object by its worker alias, and postMessage with it

06-read-window-document.js.attempt: reach the page the player is on

07-read-process-require.js.attempt: find Node: process, require, module, global, Buffer

08-read-settimeout.js.attempt: schedule work off the tick with timers, microtasks or promises

09-read-crypto-performance.js.attempt: find entropy and a high-resolution clock

10-read-importscripts-worker.js.attempt: load more code into this realm, or start a fresh unscrubbed one

11-read-websocket-xhr.js.attempt: the network by its other names

13-read-intl-sab-atomics.js.attempt: locale, shared memory, and a timer built out of them

14-this-binding.js.attempt: get the global object out of `this`, at the top level and in a plain call

15-call-eval.js.note: a strict-mode function may not have a parameter named eval; the nested sloppy/strict bootstrap in sandbox.ts is what shadows it anyway

16-new-function.js.attempt: compile a string with the Function constructor, named directly
16-new-function.js.note: only this spelling is closed by Layer 1 -- see 25

18-proxy-abi.js.attempt: wrap an ABI object in a Proxy

19-arguments-callee.js.attempt: walk the call stack through arguments.callee
19-arguments-callee.js.note: strict mode poisons callee with a throwing accessor; the throw IS the defence

20-deliberate-throw.js.attempt: nothing -- a cart that is simply broken, on purpose

21-peek-poke-bounds.js.attempt: peek and poke outside the 64 KB
21-peek-poke-bounds.js.note: machine.ts defines out-of-range peek as 0 and out-of-range poke as a no-op: a cart with an off-by-one must draw a wrong picture, not kill the machine

22-error-stack-sniff.js.attempt: read the host's stack trace out of an Error
22-error-stack-sniff.js.note: an information leak, not a capability: on V8 the string carries the runtime's frames and, in a dev build, absolute paths. Layer 2 sets Error.stackTraceLimit = 0. Nothing at Layer 1 can close it.

23-abi-tamper.js.attempt: park state on the ABI objects and replace an ABI method
23-abi-tamper.js.note: not an escape -- a determinism hole. State on `sys` survives a restore, because restore copies RAM and cannot see a property on an object. machine.ts should freeze the api objects; see the README.
23-abi-tamper.js.closedBy: unclosed: machine.ts does not freeze the api objects yet

25-function-constructor.js.note: the canonical escape. Parameter shadowing hides names; this expression uses none. Open on Layers 0+1 and the reason Layer 2 exists.

26-intrinsic-constructor-walk.js.attempt: the same escape spelled through [].constructor, "".constructor, Object.constructor and an object literal
26-intrinsic-constructor-walk.js.note: shadowing Object and Array would not help: the last spelling starts from a literal and needs no name at all

27-getprototypeof-walk.js.attempt: climb the prototype chain from values the machine handed the cart, including gfx.cls
27-getprototypeof-walk.js.note: starts from a value the ABI gave away, so no amount of care about ABI contents closes it

28-async-generator-constructors.js.attempt: the AsyncFunction, GeneratorFunction and AsyncGeneratorFunction constructors
28-async-generator-constructors.js.note: three more compilers on three more prototypes; a sandbox that neuters only Function.prototype.constructor has closed one door of four

29-constructed-dynamic-import.js.attempt: reach dynamic import through a Function-constructed body
29-constructed-dynamic-import.js.note: Layer 0 rejects the import keyword in cart source, but a string handed to the Function constructor is not cart source. The canary obtains the compiler and deliberately never calls it.

30-intrinsic-mutation.js.note: writes a unique marker rather than overwriting Array.prototype.push, because the runner shares this realm. The harness deletes the marker afterwards.

31-dynamic-import.js.attempt: import a module from cart source
31-dynamic-import.js.note: import() is syntax, not a name, so it is refused at token level before anything is compiled

33-wrapper-injection.js.attempt: close the sandbox's own wrapper and run code in its sloppy outer scope
33-wrapper-injection.js.note: found while writing this suite. A sloppy scope gives a plain call's `this` as the real global, and no Function constructor is involved, so Layer 2 would not have closed it. compileCart now compiles every source on its own as a strict function body first: a complete FunctionBody has balanced braces and cannot close one it did not open. The file is deliberately not valid JavaScript on its own.

32-control-live-global.js.attempt: NOT AN ESCAPE -- the control. Run through a doctored ABI that really does hand it a live global.
32-control-live-global.js.note: the only assertion in the suite that fails when the harness stops working rather than when the sandbox does
